corrections.text: The article states that Microsoft recommends "pinning any model obtained from an external source 'by cryptographic hash' rather than trusting a repository name." Microsoft's mitigation guidance ties cryptographic-hash pinning to fine-tuning datasets ("Pin reviewed versions by cryptographic hash"), not to models; for models, Microsoft's guidance is to "record checkpoint provenance," without the phrase "cryptographic hash" or any "repository name" framing. The "pinned by commit hash rather than referenced by repository name" language for models comes from the Cloud Security Alliance's research note, not from Microsoft.

The article quotes Microsoft as saying "Reinforcement learning recovered much of that utility while leaving attack success largely unchanged." Microsoft's actual wording is "RL recovered much of that utility while leaving attack success largely unchanged" — the abbreviation "RL" was silently expanded inside quotation marks.
